task.title: Ignore a negative or empty robots Crawl-delay
task.body:
Why: packages/seo/src/domain/robots.ts:61-62 accepts any finite Number() as Crawl-delay, so `Crawl-delay: -5` and an empty `Crawl-delay:` (Number("") is 0) become delays; a later invalid line also overwrites an earlier valid one.
Outcome: `crawlDelay(parseRobots(text), userAgent)` (src/domain/robots.ts) returns the delay only for a non-negative finite number (`0`, `2.5`, `10` are valid). A negative value (`-5`), an empty value and non-numeric text are ignored: the group keeps its earlier valid delay, or `null` when it has none. For example `User-agent: *` followed by `Crawl-delay: -5` gives `null`, and `Crawl-delay: 5` then `Crawl-delay: -1` in one group gives `5`.
Proof: the implementer adds tests in tests/domain/robots.test.ts for negative, empty, non-numeric, zero and a valid-then-invalid sequence.

spec: `crawlDelay(parseRobots(text), userAgent)` (src/domain/robots.ts) returns the delay only for a non-negative finite number (`0`, `2.5`, `10` are valid). A negative value (`-5`), an empty value and non-numeric text are ignored: the group keeps its earlier valid delay, or `null` when it has none. For example `User-agent: *` followed by `Crawl-delay: -5` gives `null`, and `Crawl-delay: 5` then `Crawl-delay: -1` in one group gives `5`.
install: npm --prefix packages/seo ci --silent && npm --prefix packages/seo run build --silent
test: cd packages/seo && npx vitest run tests/hidden/hidden.test.ts
